text_pt: E, quanto aos dez chifres, daquele mesmo reino se levantarão dez reis; e depois deles se levantará outro, o qual será diferente dos primeiros, e abaterá a três reis.
text_el: πάσης γὰρ κινήσεως κινητικώτερον σοφία διήκει δὲ καὶ χωρεῖ διὰ πάντων διὰ τὴν καθαρότητα

text_en: For she is a vapour of the power of God , and a certain pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty God : and therefore no defiled thing comes into her.
text_la: Vapor est enim virtutis Dei, et emanatio quædam est claritatis omnipotentis Dei sincera, et ideo nihil inquinatum in eam incurrit :
text_pt: E proferirá palavras contra o Altíssimo, e destruirá os santos do Altíssimo, e cuidará em mudar os tempos e a lei; e eles serão entregues na sua mão, por um tempo, e tempos, e a metade de um tempo.
text_el: ἀτμὶς γάρ ἐστιν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ δυνάμεως καὶ ἀπόρροια τῆς τοῦ παντοκράτορος δόξης εἰλικρινής διὰ τοῦτο οὐδὲν μεμιαμμένον εἰς αὐτὴν παρεμπίπτει

text_en: For she is the brightness of eternal light, and the unspotted mirror of God's majesty, and the image of his goodness .
text_la: candor est enim lucis æternæ, et speculum sine macula Dei majestatis, et imago bonitatis illius.
text_pt: Mas o juízo será estabelecido, e eles tirarão o seu domínio, para o destruir e para o desfazer até ao fim.
text_el: ἀπαύγασμα γάρ ἐστιν φωτὸς ἀϊδίου καὶ ἔσοπτρον ἀκηλίδωτον τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνεργείας καὶ εἰκὼν τῆς ἀγαθότητος αὐτοῦ

text_en: And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself the same, she renews all things, and through nations conveys herself into holy souls , she makes the friends of God and prophets .
text_la: Et cum sit una, omnia potest; et in se permanens omnia innovat : et per nationes in animas sanctas se transfert; amicos Dei et prophetas constituit.
text_pt: E o reino, e o domínio, e a majestade dos reinos debaixo de todo o céu serão dados ao povo dos santos do Altíssimo; o seu reino será um reino eterno, e todos os domínios o servirão, e lhe obedecerão.
text_el: μία δὲ οὖσα πάντα δύναται καὶ μένουσα ἐν αὑτῇ τὰ πάντα καινίζει καὶ κατὰ γενεὰς εἰς ψυχὰς ὁσίας μεταβαίνουσα φίλους θεοῦ καὶ προφήτας κατασκευάζει

text_en: For God loves none but him that dwells with wisdom.
text_la: Neminem enim diligit Deus, nisi eum qui cum sapientia inhabitat.
text_pt: Aqui terminou o assunto. Quanto a mim, Daniel, os meus pensamentos muito me perturbaram, e mudou-se em mim o meu semblante; mas guardei o assunto no meu coração.
text_el: οὐθὲν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ ὁ θεὸς εἰ μὴ τὸν σοφίᾳ συνοικοῦντα

text_en: For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of the stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it.
text_la: Est enim hæc speciosior sole, et super omnem dispositionem stellarum : luci comparata, invenitur prior.
text_el: ἔστιν γὰρ αὕτη εὐπρεπεστέρα ἡλίου καὶ ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἄστρων θέσιν φωτὶ συγκρινομένη εὑρίσκεται προτέρα

text_en: For after this comes night, but no evil can overcome wisdom.
text_la: Illi enim succedit nox; sapientiam autem non vincit malitia.
text_el: τοῦτο μὲν γὰρ διαδέχεται νύξ σοφίας δὲ οὐ κατισχύει κακία

text_en: She reaches, therefore, from end to end mightily, and orders all things sweetly.
text_la: Attingit ergo a fine usque ad finem fortiter, et disponit omnia suaviter.
text_pt: No ano terceiro do reinado do rei Belsazar apareceu-me uma visão, a mim, Daniel, depois daquela que me apareceu no princípio.
text_el: διατείνει δὲ ἀπὸ πέρατος ἐπὶ πέρας εὐρώστως καὶ διοικεῖ τὰ πάντα χρηστῶς

text_en: Her have I loved , and have sought her out from my youth, and have desired to take for my spouse, and I became a lover of her beauty.
text_la: Hanc amavi, et exquisivi a juventute mea, et quæsivi sponsam mihi eam assumere, et amator factus sum formæ illius.
text_pt: E vi na visão; e sucedeu que, quando vi, eu estava na cidadela de Susã, na província de Elão; vi, pois, na visão, que eu estava junto ao rio Ulai.
text_el: ταύτην ἐφίλησα καὶ ἐξεζήτησα ἐκ νεότητός μου καὶ ἐζήτησα νύμφην ἀγαγέσθαι ἐμαυτῷ καὶ ἐραστὴς ἐγενόμην τοῦ κάλλους αὐτῆς

text_en: She glorifies her nobility by being conversant with God : yea, and the Lord of all things has loved her.
text_la: Generositatem illius glorificat, contubernium habens Dei; sed et omnium Dominus dilexit illam.
text_pt: E levantei os meus olhos, e vi, e eis que um carneiro estava diante do rio, o qual tinha dois chifres; e os dois chifres eram altos, mas um era mais alto do que o outro; e o mais alto subiu por último.
text_el: εὐγένειαν δοξάζει συμβίωσιν θεοῦ ἔχουσα καὶ ὁ πάντων δεσπότης ἠγάπησεν αὐτήν

text_en: For it is she that teaches the knowledge of God and is the chooser of his works.
text_la: Doctrix enim est disciplinæ Dei, et electrix operum illius.
text_pt: Vi que o carneiro dava marradas para o ocidente, e para o norte e para o sul; e nenhum dos animais lhe podia resistir; nem havia quem pudesse livrar-se da sua mão; e ele fazia conforme a sua vontade, e se engrandecia.
text_el: μύστις γάρ ἐστιν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιστήμης καὶ αἱρετὶς τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ

text_en: And if riches be desired in life, what is richer than wisdom, which makes all things?
text_la: Et si divitiæ appetuntur in vita, quid sapientia locupletius quæ operatur omnia?
text_pt: E, estando eu considerando, eis que um bode vinha do ocidente sobre toda a terra, mas sem tocar no chão; e aquele bode tinha um chifre insigne entre os olhos.
text_el: εἰ δὲ πλοῦτός ἐστιν ἐπιθυμητὸν κτῆμα ἐν βίῳ τί σοφίας πλουσιώτερον τῆς τὰ πάντα ἐργαζομένης

text_en: And if sense do work: who is a more artful worker than she of those things that are?
text_la: Si autem sensus operatur, quis horum quæ sunt magis quam illa est artifex?
text_pt: E dirigiu-se ao carneiro que tinha os dois chifres, ao qual eu tinha visto em pé diante do rio, e correu contra ele no ímpeto da sua força.
text_el: εἰ δὲ φρόνησις ἐργάζεται τίς αὐτῆς τῶν ὄντων μᾶλλόν ἐστιν τεχνῖτις

text_en: And if a man love justice : her labours have great virtues : for she teaches temperance , and prudence , and justice , and fortitude , which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in life.
text_la: Et si justitiam quis diligit, labores hujus magnas habent virtutes : sobrietatem enim et prudentiam docet, et justitiam, et virtutem, quibus utilius nihil est in vita hominibus.
text_pt: E vi-o chegar perto do carneiro, enfurecido contra ele, e ferindo-o quebrou-lhe os dois chifres, pois não havia força no carneiro para lhe resistir, e o bode o lançou por terra, e o pisou aos pés; não houve quem pudesse livrar o carneiro da sua mão.
text_el: καὶ εἰ δικαιοσύνην ἀγαπᾷ τις οἱ πόνοι ταύτης εἰσὶν ἀρεταί σωφροσύνην γὰρ καὶ φρόνησιν ἐκδιδάσκει δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἀνδρείαν ὧν χρησιμώτερον οὐδέν ἐστιν ἐν βίῳ ἀνθρώποις

text_en: And if a man desire much knowledge : she knows things past, and judges of things to come: she knows the subtilties of speeches, and the solutions of arguments: she knows signs and wonders before they be done, and the events of times and ages.
text_la: Et si multitudinem scientiæ desiderat quis, scit præterita, et de futuris æstimat; scit versutias sermonum, et dissolutiones argumentorum; signa et monstra scit antequam fiant, et eventus temporum et sæculorum.
text_pt: E o bode se engrandeceu sobremaneira; mas, estando na sua maior força, aquele grande chifre foi quebrado; e no seu lugar subiram outros quatro também insignes, para os quatro ventos do céu.
text_el: εἰ δὲ καὶ πολυπειρίαν ποθεῖ τις οἶδεν τὰ ἀρχαῖα καὶ τὰ μέλλοντα εἰκάζει ἐπίσταται στροφὰς λόγων καὶ λύσεις αἰνιγμάτων σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα προγινώσκει καὶ ἐκβάσεις καιρῶν καὶ χρόνων

text_en: I purposed, therefore, to take her to me to live with me: knowing that she will communicate to me of her good things, and will be a comfort in my cares and grief.
text_la: Proposui ergo hanc adducere mihi ad convivendum, sciens quoniam mecum communicabit de bonis, et erit allocutio cogitationis et tædii mei.
text_pt: E de um deles saiu um chifre muito pequeno, o qual cresceu muito para o sul, e para o oriente, e para a terra formosa.
text_el: ἔκρινα τοίνυν ταύτην ἀγαγέσθαι πρὸς συμβίωσιν εἰδὼς ὅτι ἔσται μοι σύμβουλος ἀγαθῶν καὶ παραίνεσις φροντίδων καὶ λύπης

text_en: For her sake I shall have glory among the multitude, and honour with the ancients, though I be young:
text_la: Habebo propter hanc claritatem ad turbas, et honorem apud seniores juvenis;
text_pt: E se engrandeceu até contra o exército do céu; e a alguns do exército, e das estrelas, lançou por terra, e os pisou.
text_el: ἕξω δι' αὐτὴν δόξαν ἐν ὄχλοις καὶ τιμὴν παρὰ πρεσβυτέροις ὁ νέος

text_en: And I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of the mighty, and the faces of princes shall wonder at me.
text_la: et acutus inveniar in judicio, et in conspectu potentium admirabilis ero, et facies principum mirabuntur me :
text_pt: E se engrandeceu até contra o príncipe do exército; e por ele foi tirado o sacrifício contínuo, e o lugar do seu santuário foi lançado por terra.
text_el: ὀξὺς εὑρεθήσομαι ἐν κρίσει καὶ ἐν ὄψει δυναστῶν θαυμασθήσομαι

text_en: They shall wait for me when I hold my peace, and they shall look upon me when I speak; and if I talk much, they shall lay their hands on their mouth.
text_la: tacentem me sustinebunt, et loquentem me respicient, et sermocinante me plura, manus ori suo imponent.
text_pt: E um exército foi dado contra o sacrifício contínuo, por causa da transgressão; e lançou a verdade por terra, e o fez, e prosperou.
text_el: σιγῶντά με περιμενοῦσιν καὶ φθεγγομένῳ προσέξουσιν καὶ λαλοῦντος ἐπὶ πλεῖον χεῖρα ἐπιθήσουσιν ἐπὶ στόμα αὐτῶν

text_en: Moreover, by the means of her I shall have immortality : and shall leave behind me an everlasting memory to them that come after me.
text_la: Præterea habebo per hanc immortalitatem, et memoriam æternam his qui post me futuri sunt relinquam.
text_pt: Depois ouvi um santo que falava; e disse outro santo àquele que falava: Até quando durará a visão do sacrifício contínuo, e da transgressão assoladora, para que sejam entregues o santuário e o exército, a fim de serem pisados?
text_el: ἕξω δι' αὐτὴν ἀθανασίαν καὶ μνήμην αἰώνιον τοῖς μετ' ἐμὲ ἀπολείψω

text_en: I shall set the people in order: and nations shall be subject to me.
text_la: Disponam populos, et nationes mihi erunt subditæ :
text_pt: E ele me disse: Até duas mil e trezentas tardes e manhãs; e o santuário será purificado.
text_el: διοικήσω λαούς καὶ ἔθνη ὑποταγήσεταί μοι

text_en: Terrible kings hearing, shall be afraid of me: among the multitude I shall be found good , and valiant in war .
text_la: timebunt me audientes reges horrendi. In multitudine videbor bonus, et in bello fortis.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, havendo eu, Daniel, tido a visão, procurei o significado, e eis que se apresen- tou diante de mim como que uma semelhança de homem.
text_el: φοβηθήσονταί με ἀκούσαντες τύραννοι φρικτοί ἐν πλήθει φανοῦμαι ἀγαθὸς καὶ ἐν πολέμῳ ἀνδρεῖος

text_en: When I go into my house, I shall repose myself with her: for her conversation has no bitterness, nor her company any tediousness, but joy and gladness .
text_la: Intrans in domum meam, conquiescam cum illa : non enim habet amaritudinem conversatio illius, nec tædium convictus illius, sed lætitiam et gaudium.
text_pt: E ouvi uma voz de homem entre as margens do Ulai, a qual gritou, e disse: Gabriel, dá a entender a este a visão.
text_el: εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου προσαναπαύσομαι αὐτῇ οὐ γὰρ ἔχει πικρίαν ἡ συναναστροφὴ αὐτῆς οὐδὲ ὀδύνην ἡ συμβίωσις αὐτῆς ἀλλὰ εὐφροσύνην καὶ χαράν

text_en: Thinking these things with myself, and pondering them in my heart, that to be allied to wisdom is immortality ,
text_la: Hæc cogitans apud me et commemorans in corde meo, quoniam immortalitas est in cognatione sapientiæ,
text_pt: E veio perto de onde eu estava; e, vindo ele, me amedrontei, e caí sobre o meu rosto; mas ele me disse: Entende, filho do homem, porque esta visão acontecerá no fim do tempo.
text_el: ταῦτα λογισάμενος ἐν ἐμαυτῷ καὶ φροντίσας ἐν καρδίᾳ μου ὅτι ἀθανασία ἐστὶν ἐν συγγενείᾳ σοφίας

text_en: and that there is great delight in her friendship, and inexhaustible riches in the works of her hands, and in the exercise of conference with her, wisdom, and glory in the communication of her words: I went about seeking, that I might take her to myself.
text_la: et in amicitia illius delectatio bona, et in operibus manuum illius honestas sine defectione, et in certamine loquelæ illius sapientia, et præclaritas in communicatione sermonum ipsius : circuibam quærens, ut mihi illam assumerem.
text_pt: E, estando ele falando comigo, caí adormecido com o rosto em terra; ele, porém, me tocou, e me fez estar em pé.
text_el: καὶ ἐν φιλίᾳ αὐτῆς τέρψις ἀγαθὴ καὶ ἐν πόνοις χειρῶν αὐτῆς πλοῦτος ἀνεκλιπὴς καὶ ἐν συγγυμνασίᾳ ὁμιλίας αὐτῆς φρόνησις καὶ εὔκλεια ἐν κοινωνίᾳ λόγων αὐτῆς περιῄειν ζητῶν ὅπως λάβω αὐτὴν εἰς ἐμαυτόν

text_en: And I was a witty child, and had received a good soul .
text_la: Puer autem eram ingeniosus, et sortitus sum animam bonam.
text_pt: E disse: Eis que te farei saber o que há de acontecer no último tempo da ira; pois isso pertence ao tempo determinado do fim.
text_el: παῖς δὲ ἤμην εὐφυὴς ψυχῆς τε ἔλαχον ἀγαθῆς

text_en: And whereas I was more good , I came to a body undefiled.
text_la: Et cum essem magis bonus, veni ad corpus incoinquinatum.
text_pt: Aquele carneiro que viste com dois chifres são os reis da Média e da Pérsia,
text_el: μᾶλλον δὲ ἀγαθὸς ὢν ἦλθον εἰς σῶμα ἀμίαντον

text_en: And as I knew that I could not otherwise be continent, except God gave it, and this also was a point of wisdom, to know whose gift it was, I went to the Lord , and besought him, and said with my whole heart:
text_la: Et ut scivi quoniam aliter non possem esse continens, nisi Deus det; et hoc ipsum erat sapientiæ, scire cujus esset hoc donum : adii Dominum, et deprecatus sum illum, et dixi ex totis præcordiis meis :
text_pt: Mas o bode peludo é o rei da Grécia; e o grande chifre que tinha entre os olhos é o primeiro rei;
text_el: γνοὺς δὲ ὅτι οὐκ ἄλλως ἔσομαι ἐγκρατής ἐὰν μὴ ὁ θεὸς δῷ καὶ τοῦτο δ' ἦν φρονήσεως τὸ εἰδέναι τίνος ἡ χάρις ἐνέτυχον τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ ἐδεήθην αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπον ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας μου

text_en: God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who have made all things with your word,
text_la: Deus patrum meorum, et Domine misericordiæ, qui fecisti omnia verbo tuo,
text_pt: No ano primeiro de Dario, filho de Assuero, da linhagem dos medos, o qual foi constituído rei sobre o reino dos caldeus,

text_en: and by your wisdom have appointed man , that he should have dominion over the creature that was made by you,
text_la: et sapientia tua constituisti hominem, ut dominaretur creaturæ quæ a te facta est,
text_pt: No primeiro ano do seu reinado, eu, Daniel, entendi pelos livros que o número dos anos, de que falara o Senhor ao profeta Jeremias, em que haviam de cumprir-se as desolações de Jerusalém, era de setenta anos.

text_en: that he should order the world according to equity and justice , and execute justice with an upright heart:
text_la: ut disponat orbem terrarum in æquitate et justitia, et in directione cordis judicium judicet :
text_pt: E eu dirigi o meu rosto ao Senhor Deus, para o buscar com oração e súplicas, com jejum, e saco e cinza.

text_en: Give me wisdom, that sits by your throne, and cast me not off from among your children:
text_la: da mihi sedium tuarum assistricem sapientiam, et noli me reprobare a pueris tuis :
text_pt: E orei ao Senhor meu Deus, e confessei, e disse: Ah! Senhor! Deus grande e tremendo, que guardas a aliança e a misericórdia para com os que te amam e guardam os teus mandamentos;

text_en: For I am your servant, and the son of your handmaid, a weak man , and of short time, and falling short of the understanding of judgment and laws.
text_la: quoniam servus tuus sum ego, et filius ancillæ tuæ; homo infirmus, et exigui temporis, et minor ad intellectum judicii et legum.
text_pt: Pecamos, e cometemos iniqüidades, e procedemos impiamente, e fomos rebeldes, apartando-nos dos teus mandamentos e dos teus juízos;

text_en: For if one be perfect among the children of men , yet if your wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded.
text_la: Nam etsi quis erit consummatus inter filios hominum, si ab illo abfuerit sapientia tua, in nihilum computabitur.
text_pt: E não demos ouvidos aos teus servos, os profetas, que em teu nome falaram aos nossos reis, aos nossos príncipes, e a nossos pais, como também a todo o povo da terra.

text_en: You have chosen me to be king of your people, and a judge of your sons and daughters:
text_la: Tu elegisti me regem populo tuo, et judicem filiorum tuorum et filiarum :
text_pt: A ti, ó Senhor, pertence a justiça, mas a nós a confusão de rosto, como hoje se vê; aos homens de Judá, e aos moradores de Jerusalém, e a todo o Israel, aos de perto e aos de longe, em todas as terras por onde os tens lançado, por causa das suas rebeliões que cometeram contra ti.

text_en: And have commanded me to build a temple on your holy mount, and an altar in the city of your dwelling place, a resemblance of your holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning:
text_la: et dixisti me ædificare templum in monte sancto tuo, et in civitate habitationis tuæ altare : similitudinem tabernaculi sancti tui quod præparasti ab initio.
text_pt: Ó Senhor, a nós pertence a confusão de rosto, aos nossos reis, aos nossos príncipes, e a nossos pais, porque pecamos contra ti.

text_en: And your wisdom with you, which knows your works, which then also was present when you made the world, and knew what was agreeable to your eyes, and what was right in your commandments.
text_la: Et tecum sapientia tua, quæ novit opera tua, quæ et affuit tunc cum orbem terrarum faceres, et sciebat quid esset placitum oculis tuis, et quid directum in præceptis tuis.
text_pt: Ao Senhor, nosso Deus, pertencem a misericórdia, e o perdão; pois nos rebelamos contra ele,

text_en: Send her out of your holy heaven , and from the throne of your majesty, that she may be with me, and may labour with me, that I may know what is acceptable with you:
text_la: Mitte illam de cælis sanctis tuis, et a sede magnitudinis tuæ, ut mecum sit et mecum laboret, ut sciam quid acceptum sit apud te :
text_pt: E não obedecemos à voz do Senhor, nosso Deus, para andarmos nas suas leis, que nos deu por intermédio de seus servos, os profetas.

text_en: For she knows and understands all things, and shall lead me soberly in my works, and shall preserve me by her power.
text_la: scit enim illa omnia, et intelligit, et deducet me in operibus meis sobrie, et custodiet me in sua potentia.
text_pt: Sim, todo o Israel transgrediu a tua lei, desviando-se para não obedecer à tua voz; por isso a maldição e o juramento, que estão escritos na lei de Moisés, servo de Deus, se derramaram sobre nós; porque pecamos contra ele.

text_en: So shall my works be acceptable, and I shall govern your people justly , and shall be worthy of the throne of my father.
text_la: Et erunt accepta opera mea, et disponam populum tuum juste, et ero dignus sedium patris mei.
text_pt: E ele confirmou a sua palavra, que falou contra nós, e contra os nossos juízes que nos julgavam, trazendo sobre nós um grande mal; porquanto debaixo de todo o céu nunca se fez como se tem feito em Jerusalém.

text_en: For who among men is he that can know the counsel of God ? Or who can think what the will of God is?
text_la: Quis enim hominum poterit scire consilium Dei? aut quis poterit cogitare quid velit Deus?
text_pt: Como está escrito na lei de Moisés, todo este mal nos sobreveio; apesar disso, não suplicamos à face do Senhor nosso Deus, para nos convertermos das nossas iniqüidades, e para nos aplicarmos à tua verdade.

text_en: For the thoughts of mortal men are fearful, and our counsels uncertain.
text_la: Cogitationes enim mortalium timidæ, et incertæ providentiæ nostræ;
text_pt: Por isso o Senhor vigiou sobre o mal, e o trouxe sobre nós; porque justo é o Senhor, nosso Deus, em todas as suas obras, que fez, pois não obedecemos à sua voz.

text_en: For the corruptible body is a load upon the soul , and the earthly habitation presses down the mind that muses upon many things.
text_la: corpus enim quod corrumpitur aggravat animam, et terrena inhabitatio deprimit sensum multa cogitantem.
text_pt: Agora, pois, ó Senhor, nosso Deus, que tiraste o teu povo da terra do Egito com mão poderosa, e ganhaste para ti nome, como hoje se vê; temos pecado, temos procedido impiamente.

text_en: And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth: and with labour do we find the things that are before us. But the things that are in heaven , who shall search out?
text_la: Et difficile æstimamus quæ in terra sunt, et quæ in prospectu sunt invenimus cum labore : quæ autem in cælis sunt, quis investigabit?
text_pt: Ó Senhor, segundo todas as tuas justiças, aparte-se a tua ira e o teu furor da tua cidade de Jerusalém, do teu santo monte; porque por causa dos nossos pecados, e por causa das iniqüidades de nossos pais, tornou-se Jerusalém e o teu povo um opróbrio para todos os que estão em redor de nós.

text_en: And who shall know your thought, unless you give wisdom, and send your holy Spirit from above:
text_la: Sensum autem tuum, quis sciet, nisi tu dederis sapientiam, et miseris spiritum sanctum tuum de altissimis,
text_pt: Agora, pois, ó Deus nosso, ouve a oração do teu servo, e as suas súplicas, e sobre o teu santuário assolado faze resplandecer o teu rosto, por amor do Senhor.

text_en: And so the ways of them that are upon earth may be corrected, and men may learn the things that please you?
text_la: et sic correctæ sint semitæ eorum qui sunt in terris, et quæ tibi placent didicerint homines?
text_pt: Inclina, ó Deus meu, os teus ouvidos, e ouve; abre os teus olhos, e olha para a nossa desolação, e para a cidade que é chamada pelo teu nome, porque não lançamos as nossas súplicas perante a tua face fiados em nossas justiças, mas em tuas muitas misericórdias.

text_en: For by wisdom they were healed, whosoever have pleased you, O Lord , from the beginning.
text_la: Nam per sapientiam sanati sunt quicumque placuerunt tibi, Domine, a principio.
text_pt: Ó Senhor, ouve; ó Senhor, perdoa; ó Senhor, atende-nos e age sem tardar; por amor de ti mesmo, ó Deus meu; porque a tua cidade e o teu povo são chamados pelo teu nome.

text_en: She preserved him, that was first formed by God , the father of the world, when he was created alone,
text_la: Hæc illum qui primus formatus est a Deo patre orbis terrarum, cum solus esset creatus, custodivit,
text_pt: No terceiro ano de Ciro, rei da Pérsia, foi revelada uma palavra a Daniel, cujo nome era Beltessazar; a palavra era verdadeira e envolvia grande conflito; e ele entendeu esta palavra, e tinha entendimento da visão.
text_el: αὕτη πρωτόπλαστον πατέρα κόσμου μόνον κτισθέντα διεφύλαξεν καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ παραπτώματος ἰδίου

text_en: and she brought him out of his sin , and gave him power to govern all things.
text_la: et eduxit illum a delicto suo, et dedit illi virtutem continendi omnia.
text_pt: Naqueles dias eu, Daniel, estive triste por três semanas.
text_el: ἔδωκέν τε αὐτῷ ἰσχὺν κρατῆσαι ἁπάντων

text_en: But when the unjust went away from her in his anger , he perished by the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
text_la: Ab hac ut recessit injustus in ira sua, per iram homicidii fraterni deperiit.
text_pt: Alimento desejável não comi, nem carne nem vinho entraram na minha boca, nem me ungi com ungüento, até que se cumpriram as três semanas.
text_el: ἀποστὰς δὲ ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἄδικος ἐν ὀργῇ αὐτοῦ ἀδελφοκτόνοις συναπώλετο θυμοῖς

text_en: For whose cause, when water destroyed the earth , wisdom healed it again, directing the course of the just by contemptible wood.
text_la: Propter quem cum aqua deleret terram, sanavit iterum sapientia, per contemptibile lignum justum gubernans.
text_pt: E no dia vinte e quatro do primeiro mês eu estava à borda do grande rio Hidequel;
text_el: δι' ὃν κατακλυζομένην γῆν πάλιν ἔσωσεν σοφία δι' εὐτελοῦς ξύλου τὸν δίκαιον κυβερνήσασα

text_en: Moreover, when the nations had conspired together to consent to wickedness , she knew the just , and preserved him without blame to God , and kept him strong against the compassion for his son .
text_la: Hæc et in consensu nequitiæ, cum se nationes contulissent, scivit justum, et conservavit sine querela Deo, et in filii misericordia fortem custodivit.
text_pt: E levantei os meus olhos, e olhei, e eis um homem vestido de linho, e os seus lombos cingidos com ouro fino de Ufaz;
text_el: αὕτη καὶ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ πονηρίας ἐθνῶν συγχυθέντων ἔγνω τὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἐτήρησεν αὐτὸν ἄμεμπτον θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τέκνου σπλάγχνοις ἰσχυρὸν ἐφύλαξεν

text_en: She delivered the just man , who fled from the wicked that were perishing, when the fire came down upon Pentapolis :
text_la: Hæc justum a pereuntibus impiis liberavit fugientem, descendente igne in Pentapolim :
text_pt: E o seu corpo era como berilo, e o seu rosto parecia um relâmpago, e os seus olhos como tochas de fogo, e os seus braços e os seus pés brilhavam como bronze polido; e a voz das suas palavras era como a voz de uma multidão.
text_el: αὕτη δίκαιον ἐξαπολλυμένων ἀσεβῶν ἐρρύσατο φυγόντα καταβάσιον πῦρ Πενταπόλεως

text_en: Whose land, for a testimony of their wickedness , is desolate, and smokes to this day, and the trees bear fruits that ripen not, and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an incredulous soul .
text_la: quibus in testimonium nequitiæ fumigabunda constat deserta terra, et incerto tempore fructus habentes arbores : et incredibilis animæ memoria stans figmentum salis.
text_pt: E só eu, Daniel, tive aquela visão. Os homens que estavam comigo não a viram; contudo caiu sobre eles um grande temor, e fugiram, escondendo-se.
text_el: ἧς ἔτι μαρτύριον τῆς πονηρίας καπνιζομένη καθέστηκε χέρσος καὶ ἀτελέσιν ὥραις καρποφοροῦντα φυτά ἀπιστούσης ψυχῆς μνημεῖον ἑστηκυῖα στήλη ἁλός

text_en: For regarding not wisdom, they did not only slip in this, that they were ignorant of good things; but they left also unto men a memorial of their folly, so that in the things in which they sinned , they could not so much as lie hid.
text_la: Sapientiam enim prætereuntes, non tantum in hoc lapsi sunt ut ignorarent bona, sed et insipientiæ suæ reliquerunt hominibus memoriam, ut in his quæ peccaverunt nec latere potuissent.
text_pt: Fiquei, pois, eu só, a contemplar esta grande visão, e não ficou força em mim; transmudou-se o meu semblante em corrupção, e não tive força alguma.
text_el: σοφίαν γὰρ παροδεύσαντες οὐ μόνον ἐβλάβησαν τοῦ μὴ γνῶναι τὰ καλά ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀφροσύνης ἀπέλιπον τῷ βίῳ μνημόσυνον ἵνα ἐν οἷς ἐσφάλησαν μηδὲ λαθεῖν δυνηθῶσιν

text_en: But wisdom has delivered from sorrow them that attend upon her.
text_la: Sapientia autem hos qui se observant a doloribus liberavit.
text_pt: Contudo ouvi a voz das suas palavras; e, ouvindo o som das suas palavras, eu caí sobre o meu rosto num profundo sono, com o meu rosto em terra.
text_el: σοφία δὲ τοὺς θεραπεύοντας αὐτὴν ἐκ πόνων ἐρρύσατο

text_en: She conducted the just , when he fled from his brother's wrath , through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God , and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.
text_la: Hæc profugum iræ fratris justum deduxit per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum; honestavit illum in laboribus, et complevit labores illius.
text_pt: E eis que certa mão me tocou, e fez com que me movesse sobre os meus joelhos e sobre as palmas das minhas mãos.
text_el: αὕτη φυγάδα ὀργῆς ἀδελφοῦ δίκαιον ὡδήγησεν ἐν τρίβοις εὐθείαις ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ βασιλείαν θεοῦ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ γνῶσιν ἁγίων εὐπόρησεν αὐτὸν ἐν μόχθοις καὶ ἐπλήθυνεν τοὺς πόνους αὐτοῦ

text_en: In the deceit of them that overreached him, she stood by him, and made him honourable .
text_la: In fraude circumvenientium illum affuit illi, et honestum fecit illum.
text_pt: E me disse: Daniel, homem muito amado, entende as palavras que vou te dizer, e levanta-te sobre os teus pés, porque a ti sou enviado. E, falando ele comigo esta palavra, levantei-me tremendo.
text_el: ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ κατισχυόντων αὐτὸν παρέστη καὶ ἐπλούτισεν αὐτόν

text_en: She kept him safe from his enemies, and she defended him from seducers, and gave him a strong conflict, that he might overcome, and know that wisdom is mightier than all.
text_la: Custodivit illum ab inimicis, et a seductoribus tutavit illum : et certamen forte dedit illi ut vinceret, et sciret quoniam omnium potentior est sapientia.
text_pt: Então me disse: Não temas, Daniel, porque desde o primeiro dia em que aplicaste o teu coração a compreender e a humilhar-te perante o teu Deus, são ouvidas as tuas palavras; e eu vim por causa das tuas palavras.
text_el: διεφύλαξεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ ἐχθρῶν καὶ ἀπὸ ἐνεδρευόντων ἠσφαλίσατο καὶ ἀγῶνα ἰσχυρὸν ἐβράβευσεν αὐτῷ ἵνα γνῷ ὅτι παντὸς δυνατωτέρα ἐστὶν εὐσέβεια

text_en: She forsook not the just when he was sold, but delivered him from sinners: she went down with him into the pit.
text_la: Hæc venditum justum non dereliquit, sed a peccatoribus liberavit eum; descenditque cum illo in foveam,
text_pt: Mas o príncipe do reino da Pérsia me resistiu vinte e um dias, e eis que Miguel, um dos primeiros príncipes, veio para ajudar-me, e eu fiquei ali com os reis da Pérsia.
text_el: αὕτη πραθέντα δίκαιον οὐκ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀλλὰ ἐξ ἁμαρτίας ἐρρύσατο αὐτόν

text_en: And in bands she left him not, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: and showed them to be liars that had accused him, and gave him everlasting glory .
text_la: et in vinculis non dereliquit illum, donec afferret illi sceptrum regni, et potentiam adversus eos qui eum deprimebant : et mendaces ostendit qui maculaverunt illum, et dedit illi claritatem æternam.
text_pt: Agora vim, para fazer-te entender o que há de acontecer ao teu povo nos derradeiros dias; porque a visão é ainda para muitos dias.
text_el: συγκατέβη αὐτῷ εἰς λάκκον καὶ ἐν δεσμοῖς οὐκ ἀφῆκεν αὐτόν ἕως ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ σκῆπτρα βασιλείας καὶ ἐξουσίαν τυραννούντων αὐτοῦ ψευδεῖς τε ἔδειξεν τοὺς μωμησαμένους αὐτὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ δόξαν αἰώνιον

text_en: She delivered the just people, and blameless seed, from the nations that oppressed them.
text_la: Hæc populum justum et semen sine querela liberavit a nationibus quæ illum deprimebant.
text_pt: E, falando ele comigo estas palavras, abaixei o meu rosto para a terra, e emudeci.
text_el: αὕτη λαὸν ὅσιον καὶ σπέρμα ἄμεμπτον ἐρρύσατο ἐξ ἔθνους θλιβόντων

text_en: She entered into the soul of the servant of God and stood against dreadful kings in wonders and signs .
text_la: Intravit in animam servi Dei, et stetit contra reges horrendos in portentis et signis.
text_pt: E eis que alguém, semelhante aos filhos dos homens, tocou-me os lábios; então abri a minha boca, e falei, dizendo àquele que estava em pé diante de mim: senhor meu, por causa da visão sobrevieram-me dores, e não me ficou força alguma.
text_el: εἰσῆλθεν εἰς ψυχὴν θεράποντος κυρίου καὶ ἀντέστη βασιλεῦσιν φοβεροῖς ἐν τέρασι καὶ σημείοις

text_en: And she rendered to the just the wages of their labours, and conducted them in a wonderful way: and she was to them for a covert by day, and for the light of stars by night:
text_la: Et reddidit justis mercedem laborum suorum, et deduxit illos in via mirabili : et fuit illis in velamento diei, et in luce stellarum per noctem;
text_pt: Como, pois, pode o servo do meu senhor falar com o meu senhor? Porque, quanto a mim, desde agora não resta força em mim, e nem fôlego ficou em mim.
text_el: ἀπέδωκεν ὁσίοις μισθὸν κόπων αὐτῶν ὡδήγησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν ὁδῷ θαυμαστῇ καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῖς εἰς σκέπην ἡμέρας καὶ εἰς φλόγα ἄστρων τὴν νύκτα

text_en: And she brought them through the Red Sea , and carried them over through a great water.
text_la: transtulit illos per mare Rubrum, et transvexit illos per aquam nimiam.
text_pt: E aquele, que tinha aparência de um homem, tocou-me outra vez, e fortaleceu-me.
text_el: διεβίβασεν αὐτοὺς θάλασσαν ἐρυθρὰν καὶ διήγαγεν αὐτοὺς δι' ὕδατος πολλοῦ

text_en: But their enemies she drowned in the sea, and from the depth of hell she brought them out. Therefore the just took the spoils of the wicked .
text_la: Inimicos autem illorum demersit in mare, et ab altitudine inferorum eduxit illos. Ideo justi tulerunt spolia impiorum,
text_pt: E disse: Não temas, homem muito amado, paz seja contigo; anima-te, sim, anima-te. E, falando ele comigo, fiquei fortalecido, e disse: Fala, meu senhor, porque me fortaleceste.
text_el: τοὺς δὲ ἐχθροὺς αὐτῶν κατέκλυσεν καὶ ἐκ βάθους ἀβύσσου ἀνέβρασεν αὐτούς

text_en: And they sung to your holy name , O Lord , and they praised with one accord your victorious hand.
text_la: et decantaverunt, Domine, nomen sanctum tuum, et victricem manum tuam laudaverunt pariter :
text_pt: E ele disse: Sabes por que eu vim a ti? Agora, pois, tornarei a pelejar contra o príncipe dos persas; e, saindo eu, eis que virá o príncipe da Grécia.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο δίκαιοι ἐσκύλευσαν ἀσεβεῖς καὶ ὕμνησαν κύριε τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ἅγιόν σου τήν τε ὑπέρμαχόν σου χεῖρα ᾔνεσαν ὁμοθυμαδόν

text_en: For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, and made the tongues of infants eloquent.
text_la: quoniam sapientia aperuit os mutorum, et linguas infantium fecit disertas.
text_pt: Mas eu te declararei o que está registrado na escritura da verdade; e ninguém há que me anime contra aqueles, senão Miguel, vosso príncipe.
text_el: ὅτι ἡ σοφία ἤνοιξεν στόμα κωφῶν καὶ γλώσσας νηπίων ἔθηκεν τρανάς

text_en: She prospered their works in the hands of the holy prophet .
text_la: Direxit opera eorum in manibus prophetæ sancti.
text_pt: Eu, pois, no primeiro ano de Dario, o medo, levantei-me para animá-lo e fortalecê-lo.
text_el: εὐόδωσεν τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ἐν χειρὶ προφήτου ἁγίου

text_en: They went through wildernesses that were not inhabited, and in desert places they pitched their tents.
text_la: Iter fecerunt per deserta quæ non habitabantur, et in locis desertis fixerunt casas.
text_pt: E agora te declararei a verdade: Eis que ainda três reis estarão na Pérsia, e o quarto acumulará grandes riquezas, mais do que todos; e, tornando-se forte, por suas riquezas, suscitará a todos contra o reino da Grécia.
text_el: διώδευσαν ἔρημον ἀοίκητον καὶ ἐν ἀβάτοις ἔπηξαν σκηνάς

text_en: They stood against their enemies, and revenged themselves of their adversaries.
text_la: Steterunt contra hostes, et de inimicis se vindicaverunt.
text_pt: Depois se levantará um rei valente, que reinará com grande domínio, e fará o que lhe aprouver.
text_el: ἀντέστησαν πολεμίοις καὶ ἐχθροὺς ἠμύναντο

text_en: They were thirsty, and they called upon you, and water was given them out of the high rock, and a refreshment of their thirst out of the hard stone.
text_la: Sitierunt, et invocaverunt te, et data est illis aqua de petra altissima, et requies sitis de lapide duro.
text_pt: Mas, estando ele em pé, o seu reino será quebrado, e será repartido para os quatro ventos do céu; mas não para a sua posteridade, nem tampouco segundo o seu domínio com que reinou, porque o seu reino será arrancado, e passará a outros que não eles.
text_el: ἐδίψησαν καὶ ἐπεκαλέσαντό σε καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἐκ πέτρας ἀκροτόμου ὕδωρ καὶ ἴαμα δίψης ἐκ λίθου σκληροῦ

text_en: For by what things their enemies were punished, when their drink failed them, while the children of Israel abounded therewith, and rejoiced:
text_la: Per quæ enim pœnas passi sunt inimici illorum a defectione potus sui, et in eis cum abundarent filii Israël lætati sunt :
text_pt: E será forte o rei do sul; mas um dos seus príncipes será mais forte do que ele, e reinará poderosamente; seu domínio será grande.

text_en: By the same things they in their need were benefited.
text_la: per hæc, cum illis deessent, bene cum illis actum est.
text_pt: Mas, ao fim de alguns anos, eles se aliarão; e a filha do rei do sul virá ao rei do norte para fazer um tratado; mas ela não reterá a força do seu braço; nem ele persistirá, nem o seu braço, porque ela será entregue, e os que a tiverem trazido, e seu pai, e o que a fortalecia naqueles tempos.
text_el: δι' ὧν γὰρ ἐκολάσθησαν οἱ ἐχθροὶ αὐτῶν διὰ τούτων αὐτοὶ ἀποροῦντες εὐεργετήθησαν

text_en: For instead of a fountain of an ever running river, you gave human blood to the unjust .
text_la: Nam pro fonte quidem sempiterni fluminis, humanum sanguinem dedisti injustis.
text_pt: Mas de um renovo das raízes dela um se levantará em seu lugar, e virá com o exército, e entrará na fortaleza do rei do norte, e operará contra eles, e prevalecerá.
text_el: ἀντὶ μὲν πηγῆς ἀενάου ποταμοῦ αἵματι λυθρώδει ταραχθέντος

text_en: And whilst they were diminished for a manifest reproof of their murdering the infants, you gave to yours abundant water unlooked for:
text_la: Qui cum minuerentur in traductione infantium occisorum, dedisti illis abundantem aquam insperate,
text_pt: Também os seus deuses com as suas imagens de fundição, com os seus objetos preciosos de prata e ouro, levará cativos para o Egito; e por alguns anos ele persistirá contra o rei do norte.
text_el: εἰς ἔλεγχον νηπιοκτόνου διατάγματος ἔδωκας αὐτοῖς δαψιλὲς ὕδωρ ἀνελπίστως

text_en: Showing by the thirst that was then, how you exalted yours, and killed their adversaries.
text_la: ostendens per sitim quæ tunc fuit, quemadmodum tuos exaltares, et adversarios illorum necares.
text_pt: E entrará no reino o rei do sul, e tornará para a sua terra.
text_el: δείξας διὰ τοῦ τότε δίψους πῶς τοὺς ὑπεναντίους ἐκόλασας

text_en: For when they were tried, and chastised with mercy, they knew how the wicked were judged with wrath , and tormented.
text_la: Cum enim tentati sunt, et quidem cum misericordia disciplinam accipientes, scierunt quemadmodum cum ira judicati impii tormenta paterentur.
text_pt: Mas seus filhos intervirão e reunirão uma multidão de grandes forças; e virá apressadamente e inundará, e passará adiante; e, voltando levará a guerra até a sua fortaleza.
text_el: ὅτε γὰρ ἐπειράσθησαν καίπερ ἐν ἐλέει παιδευόμενοι ἔγνωσαν πῶς μετ' ὀργῆς κρινόμενοι ἀσεβεῖς ἐβασανίζοντο

text_en: For you admonished and tried them as a father: but the others, as a severe king, you examined and condemned.
text_la: Hos quidem tamquam pater monens probasti; illos autem tamquam durus rex interrogans condemnasti.
text_pt: Então o rei do sul se exasperará, e sairá, e pelejará contra ele, contra o rei do norte; este porá em campo grande multidão, e aquela multidão será entregue na sua mão.
text_el: τούτους μὲν γὰρ ὡς πατὴρ νουθετῶν ἐδοκίμασας ἐκείνους δὲ ὡς ἀπότομος βασιλεὺς καταδικάζων ἐξήτασας

text_en: For whether absent or present, they were tormented alike.
text_la: Absentes enim, et præsentes, similiter torquebantur.
text_pt: A multidão será tirada e o seu coração se elevará; mas ainda que derrubará muitos milhares, contudo não prevalecerá.
text_el: καὶ ἀπόντες δὲ καὶ παρόντες ὁμοίως ἐτρύχοντο

text_en: For a double affliction came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past.
text_la: Duplex enim illos acceperat tædium et gemitus, cum memoria præteritorum.
text_pt: Porque o rei do norte tornará, e porá em campo uma multidão maior do que a primeira, e ao fim dos tempos, isto é, de anos, virá à pressa com grande exército e com muitas riquezas.
text_el: διπλῆ γὰρ αὐτοὺς ἔλαβεν λύπη καὶ στεναγμὸς μνημῶν τῶν παρελθόντων

text_en: For when they heard that by their punishments the others were benefited, they remembered the Lord , wondering at the end of what had come to pass.
text_la: Cum enim audirent per sua tormenta bene secum agi, commemorati sunt Dominum, admirantes in finem exitus.
text_pt: E, naqueles tempos, muitos se levantarão contra o rei do sul; e os violentos dentre o teu povo se levantarão para cumprir a visão, mas eles cairão.
text_el: ὅτε γὰρ ἤκουσαν διὰ τῶν ἰδίων κολάσεων εὐεργετημένους αὐτούς ᾔσθοντο τοῦ κυρίου

text_en: For whom they scorned before, when he was thrown out at the time of his being wickedly exposed to perish, him they admired in the end, when they saw the event: their thirsting being unlike to that of the just .
text_la: Quem enim in expositione prava projectum deriserunt, in finem eventus mirati sunt, non similiter justis sitientes.
text_pt: E o rei do norte virá, e levantará baluartes, e tomará a cidade forte; e os braços do sul não poderão resistir, nem o seu povo escolhido, pois não haverá força para resistir.
text_el: ὃν γὰρ ἐν ἐκθέσει πάλαι ῥιφέντα ἀπεῖπον χλευάζοντες ἐπὶ τέλει τῶν ἐκβάσεων ἐθαύμασαν οὐχ ὅμοια δικαίοις διψήσαντες

text_en: But for the foolish devices of their iniquity, because some being deceived worshipped dumb serpents and worthless beasts, you sent upon them a multitude of dumb beasts for vengeance:
text_la: Pro cogitationibus autem insensatis iniquitatis illorum, quod quidam errantes colebant mutos serpentes et bestias supervacuas, immisisti illis multitudinem mutorum animalium in vindictam;
text_pt: O que, pois, há de vir contra ele fará segundo a sua vontade, e ninguém poderá resistir diante dele; e estará na terra gloriosa, e por sua mão haverá destruição.
text_el: ἀντὶ δὲ λογισμῶν ἀσυνέτων ἀδικίας αὐτῶν ἐν οἷς πλανηθέντες ἐθρήσκευον ἄλογα ἑρπετὰ καὶ κνώδαλα εὐτελῆ ἐπαπέστειλας αὐτοῖς πλῆθος ἀλόγων ζῴων εἰς ἐκδίκησιν

text_en: That they might know that by what things a man sins , by the same also he is tormented.
text_la: ut scirent quia per quæ peccat quis, per hæc et torquetur.
text_pt: E dirigirá o seu rosto, para vir com a potência de todo o seu reino, e com ele os retos, assim ele fará; e lhe dará uma filha das mulheres, para corrompê-la; ela, porém, não subsistirá, nem será para ele.
text_el: ἵνα γνῶσιν ὅτι δι' ὧν τις ἁμαρτάνει διὰ τούτων κολάζεται

text_en: For your almighty hand, which made the world of matter without form, was not unable to send upon them a multitude of bears, or fierce lions,
text_la: Non enim impossibilis erat omnipotens manus tua, quæ creavit orbem terrarum ex materia invisa, immittere illis multitudinem ursorum, aut audaces leones,
text_pt: Depois virará o seu rosto para as ilhas, e tomará muitas; mas um príncipe fará cessar o seu opróbrio contra ele, e ainda fará recair sobre ele o seu opróbrio.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ ἠπόρει ἡ παντοδύναμός σου χεὶρ καὶ κτίσασα τὸν κόσμον ἐξ ἀμόρφου ὕλης ἐπιπέμψαι αὐτοῖς πλῆθος ἄρκων ἢ θρασεῖς λέοντας

text_en: or unknown beasts of a new kind, full of rage; either breathing out a fiery vapour, or sending forth a stinking smoke, or shooting horrible sparks out of their eyes:
text_la: aut novi generis ira plenas ignotas bestias, aut vaporem ignium spirantes, aut fumi odorem proferentes, aut horrendas ab oculis scintillas emittentes;
text_pt: Virará então o seu rosto para as fortalezas da sua própria terra, mas tropeçará, e cairá, e não será achado.
text_el: ἢ νεοκτίστους θυμοῦ πλήρεις θῆρας ἀγνώστους ἤτοι πυρπνόον φυσῶντας ἄσθμα ἢ βρόμον λικμωμένους καπνοῦ ἢ δεινοὺς ἀπ' ὀμμάτων σπινθῆρας ἀστράπτοντας

text_en: Whereof not only the hurt might be able to destroy them, but also the very sight might kill them through fear.
text_la: quarum non solum læsura poterat illos exterminare, sed et aspectus per timorem occidere.
text_pt: E em seu lugar se levantará quem fará passar um arrecadador pela glória do reino; mas em poucos dias será quebrantado, e isto sem ira e sem batalha.
text_el: ὧν οὐ μόνον ἡ βλάβη ἠδύνατο συνεκτρῖψαι αὐτούς ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ ὄψις ἐκφοβήσασα διολέσαι

text_en: Yea, and without these, they might have been slain with one blast, persecuted by their own deeds, and scattered by the breath of your power: but you have ordered all things in measure, and number, and weight.
text_la: Sed et sine his uno spiritu poterant occidi, persecutionem passi ab ipsis factis suis, et dispersi per spiritum virtutis tuæ : sed omnia in mensura, et numero et pondere disposuisti.
text_pt: Depois se levantará em seu lugar um homem vil, ao qual não tinham dado a dignidade real; mas ele virá caladamente, e tomará o reino com engano.
text_el: καὶ χωρὶς δὲ τούτων ἑνὶ πνεύματι πεσεῖν ἐδύναντο ὑπὸ τῆς δίκης διωχθέντες καὶ λικμηθέντες ὑπὸ πνεύματος δυνάμεώς σου ἀλλὰ πάντα μέτρῳ καὶ ἀριθμῷ καὶ σταθμῷ διέταξας

text_en: For great power always belonged to you alone: and who shall resist the strength of your arm?
text_la: Multum enim valere, tibi soli supererat semper : et virtuti brachii tui quis resistet?
text_pt: E com os braços de uma inundação serão varridos de diante dele; e serão quebrantados, como também o príncipe da aliança.
text_el: τὸ γὰρ μεγάλως ἰσχύειν σοι πάρεστιν πάντοτε καὶ κράτει βραχίονός σου τίς ἀντιστήσεται

text_en: For the whole world before you is as the least grain of the balance, and as a drop of the morning dew, that falls down upon the earth.
text_la: Quoniam tamquam momentum stateræ, sic est ante te orbis terrarum, et tamquam gutta roris antelucani quæ descendit in terram.
text_pt: E, depois do concerto com ele, usará de engano; e subirá, e se tornará forte com pouca gente.
text_el: ὅτι ὡς ῥοπὴ ἐκ πλαστίγγων ὅλος ὁ κόσμος ἐναντίον σου καὶ ὡς ῥανὶς δρόσου ὀρθρινὴ κατελθοῦσα ἐπὶ γῆν

text_en: But you have mercy upon all, because you can do all things, and overlook the sins of men for the sake of repentance.
text_la: Sed misereris omnium, quia omnia potes; et dissimulas peccata hominum, propter pœnitentiam.
text_pt: Virá também caladamente aos lugares mais férteis da província, e fará o que nunca fizeram seus pais, nem os pais de seus pais; repartirá entre eles a presa e os despojos, e os bens, e formará os seus projetos contra as fortalezas, mas por certo tempo.
text_el: ἐλεεῖς δὲ πάντας ὅτι πάντα δύνασαι καὶ παρορᾷς ἁμαρτήματα ἀνθρώπων εἰς μετάνοιαν

text_en: For you love all things that are, and hate none of the things which you have made : for you did not appoint, or make anything hating it.
text_la: Diligis enim omnia quæ sunt, et nihil odisti eorum quæ fecisti; nec enim odiens aliquid constituisti aut fecisti.
text_pt: E suscitará a sua força e a sua coragem contra o rei do sul com um grande exército; e o rei do sul se envolverá na guerra com um grande e mui poderoso exército; mas não subsistirá, porque maquinarão projetos contra ele.
text_el: ἀγαπᾷς γὰρ τὰ ὄντα πάντα καὶ οὐδὲν βδελύσσῃ ὧν ἐποίησας οὐδὲ γὰρ ἂν μισῶν τι κατεσκεύασας

text_en: And how could anything endure, if you would not? Or be preserved, if not called by you?
text_la: Quomodo autem posset aliquid permanere, nisi tu voluisses? aut quod a te vocatum non esset conservaretur?
text_pt: E os que comerem os seus alimentos o destruirão; e o exército dele será arrasado, e cairão muitos mortos.
text_el: πῶς δὲ διέμεινεν ἄν τι εἰ μὴ σὺ ἠθέλησας ἢ τὸ μὴ κληθὲν ὑπὸ σοῦ διετηρήθη

text_en: But you spare all: because they are yours, O Lord , who love souls .
text_la: Parcis autem omnibus, quoniam tua sunt, Domine, qui amas animas.
text_pt: Também estes dois reis terão o coração atento para fazerem o mal, e a uma mesma mesa falarão a mentira; mas isso não prosperará, porque ainda verá o fim no tempo determinado.
text_el: φείδῃ δὲ πάντων ὅτι σά ἐστιν δέσποτα φιλόψυχε

text_en: O how good and sweet is your Spirit, O Lord , in all things!
text_la: O quam bonus et suavis est, Domine, spiritus tuus in omnibus!
text_pt: E naquele tempo se levantará Miguel, o grande príncipe, que se levanta a favor dos filhos do teu povo, e haverá um tempo de angústia, qual nunca houve, desde que houve nação até àquele tempo; mas naquele tempo livrar-se-á o teu povo, todo aquele que for achado escrito no livro.
text_el: τὸ γὰρ ἄφθαρτόν σου πνεῦμά ἐστιν ἐν πᾶσιν

text_en: And therefore you chastise them that err , by little and little: and admonish them, and speak to them, concerning the things wherein they offend: that leaving their wickedness , they may believe in you, O Lord .
text_la: Ideoque eos qui exerrant partibus corripis, et de quibus peccant admones et alloqueris, ut relicta malitia credant in te, Domine.
text_pt: E muitos dos que dormem no pó da terra ressuscitarão, uns para vida eterna, e outros para vergonha e desprezo eterno.
text_el: διὸ τοὺς παραπίπτοντας κατ' ὀλίγον ἐλέγχεις καὶ ἐν οἷς ἁμαρτάνουσιν ὑπομιμνῄσκων νουθετεῖς ἵνα ἀπαλλαγέντες τῆς κακίας πιστεύσωσιν ἐπὶ σέ κύριε

text_en: For those ancient inhabitants of your holy land, whom you abhorred,
text_la: Illos enim antiquos inhabitatores terræ sanctæ tuæ, quos exhorruisti,
text_pt: Os que forem sábios, pois, resplandecerão como o fulgor do firmamento; e os que a muitos ensinam a justiça, como as estrelas sempre e eternamente.
text_el: καὶ γὰρ τοὺς πάλαι οἰκήτορας τῆς ἁγίας σου γῆς

text_en: because they did works hateful to you by their sorceries, and wicked sacrifices ,
text_la: quoniam odibilia opera tibi faciebant per medicamina et sacrificia injusta,
text_pt: E tu, Daniel, encerra estas palavras e sela este livro, até ao fim do tempo; muitos correrão de uma parte para outra, e o conhecimento se multiplicará.
text_el: μισήσας ἐπὶ τῷ ἔχθιστα πράσσειν ἔργα φαρμακειῶν καὶ τελετὰς ἀνοσίους

text_en: and those merciless murderers of their own children, and eaters of men's bowels, and devourers of blood from the midst of your consecration ,
text_la: et filiorum suorum necatores sine misericordia, et comestores viscerum hominum, et devoratores sanguinis a medio sacramento tuo,
text_pt: Então eu, Daniel, olhei, e eis que estavam em pé outros dois, um deste lado, à beira do rio, e o outro do outro lado, à beira do rio.
text_el: τέκνων τε φονὰς ἀνελεήμονας καὶ σπλαγχνοφάγον ἀνθρωπίνων σαρκῶν θοῖναν καὶ αἵματος ἐκ μέσου μύστας θιάσου

text_en: and those parents sacrificing with their own hands helpless souls , it was your will to destroy by the hands of our parents ,
text_la: et auctores parentes animarum inauxiliatarum, perdere voluisti per manus parentum nostrorum :
text_pt: E ele disse ao homem vestido de linho, que estava sobre as águas do rio: Quando será o fim destas maravilhas?
text_el: καὶ αὐθέντας γονεῖς ψυχῶν ἀβοηθήτων ἐβουλήθης ἀπολέσαι διὰ χειρῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν

text_en: that the land which of all is most dear to you, might receive a worthy colony of the children of God .
text_la: ut dignam perciperent peregrinationem puerorum Dei, quæ tibi omnium carior est terra.
text_pt: E ouvi o homem vestido de linho, que estava sobre as águas do rio, o qual levantou ao céu a sua mão direita e a sua mão esquerda, e jurou por aquele que vive eternamente que isso seria para um tempo, tempos e metade do tempo, e quando tiverem acabado de espalhar o poder do povo santo, todas estas coisas serão cumpridas.
text_el: ἵνα ἀξίαν ἀποικίαν δέξηται θεοῦ παίδων ἡ παρὰ σοὶ πασῶν τιμιωτάτη γῆ

text_en: Yet even those you spared as men , and sent wasps forerunners of your host, to destroy them by little and little.
text_la: Sed et his tamquam hominibus pepercisti, et misisti antecessores exercitus tui vespas, ut illos paulatim exterminarent.
text_pt: Eu, pois, ouvi, mas não entendi; por isso eu disse: Senhor meu, qual será o fim destas coisas?
text_el: ἀλλὰ καὶ τούτων ὡς ἀνθρώπων ἐφείσω ἀπέστειλάς τε προδρόμους τοῦ στρατοπέδου σου σφῆκας ἵνα αὐτοὺς κατὰ βραχὺ ἐξολεθρεύσωσιν

text_en: Not that you were unable to bring the wicked under the just by war , or by cruel beasts, or with one rough word to destroy them at once:
text_la: Non quia impotens eras in bello subjicere impios justis, aut bestiis sævis, aut verbo duro simul exterminare :
text_pt: E ele disse: Vai, Daniel, porque estas palavras estão fechadas e seladas até ao tempo do fim.
text_el: οὐκ ἀδυνατῶν ἐν παρατάξει ἀσεβεῖς δικαίοις ὑποχειρίους δοῦναι ἢ θηρίοις δεινοῖς ἢ λόγῳ ἀποτόμῳ ὑφ' ἓν ἐκτρῖψαι

text_en: But executing your judgments by degrees, you gave them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a wicked generation , and their malice natural, and that their thought could never be changed.
text_la: sed partibus judicans, dabas locum pœnitentiæ, non ignorans quoniam nequam est natio eorum, et naturalis malitia ipsorum, et quoniam non poterat mutari cogitatio illorum in perpetuum.
text_pt: Muitos serão purificados, e embranquecidos, e provados; mas os ímpios procederão impiamente, e nenhum dos ímpios entenderá, mas os sábios entenderão.
text_el: κρίνων δὲ κατὰ βραχὺ ἐδίδους τόπον μετανοίας οὐκ ἀγνοῶν ὅτι πονηρὰ ἡ γένεσις αὐτῶν καὶ ἔμφυτος ἡ κακία αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἀλλαγῇ ὁ λογισμὸς αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

text_en: For it was a cursed seed from the beginning: neither did you for fear of any one give pardon to their sins .
text_la: Semen enim erat maledictum ab initio; nec timens aliquem, veniam dabas peccatis illorum.
text_pt: E desde o tempo em que o sacrifício contínuo for tirado, e posta a abominação desoladora, haverá mil duzentos e noventa dias.
text_el: σπέρμα γὰρ ἦν κατηραμένον ἀπ' ἀρχῆς οὐδὲ εὐλαβούμενός τινα ἐφ' οἷς ἡμάρτανον ἄδειαν ἐδίδους

text_en: For who shall say to you: What have you done? Or who shall withstand your judgment? Or who shall come before you to be a revenger of wicked men ? Or who shall accuse you, if the nations perish, which you have made?
text_la: Quis enim dicet tibi : Quid fecisti? aut quis stabit contra judicium tuum? aut quis in conspectu tuo veniet vindex iniquorum hominum? aut quis tibi imputabit, si perierint nationes quas tu fecisti?
text_pt: Bem-aventurado o que espera e chega até mil trezentos e trinta e cinco dias.
text_el: τίς γὰρ ἐρεῖ τί ἐποίησας ἢ τίς ἀντιστήσεται τῷ κρίματί σου τίς δὲ ἐγκαλέσει σοι κατὰ ἐθνῶν ἀπολωλότων ἃ σὺ ἐποίησας ἢ τίς εἰς κατάστασίν σοι ἐλεύσεται ἔκδικος κατὰ ἀδίκων ἀνθρώπων

text_en: For there is no other God but you, who have care of all, that you should show that you do not give judgment unjustly .
text_la: Non enim est alius deus quam tu, cui cura est de omnibus, ut ostendas quoniam non injuste judicas judicium.
text_pt: Tu, porém, vai até ao fim; porque descansarás, e te levantarás na tua herança, no fim dos dias.
text_el: οὔτε γὰρ θεός ἐστιν πλὴν σοῦ ᾧ μέλει περὶ πάντων ἵνα δείξῃς ὅτι οὐκ ἀδίκως ἔκρινας

text_en: Neither shall king, nor tyrant, in your sight inquire about them whom you have destroyed.
text_la: Neque rex, neque tyrannus in conspectu tuo inquirent de his quos perdidisti.
text_el: οὔτε βασιλεὺς ἢ τύραννος ἀντοφθαλμῆσαι δυνήσεταί σοι περὶ ὧν ἐκόλασας

text_en: For so much then, as you are just , you order all things justly : thinking it not agreeable to the power, to condemn him who deserves not to be punished.
text_la: Cum ergo sis justus, juste omnia disponis; ipsum quoque qui non debet puniri, condemnare, exterum æstimas a tua virtute.
text_el: δίκαιος δὲ ὢν δικαίως τὰ πάντα διέπεις αὐτὸν τὸν μὴ ὀφείλοντα κολασθῆναι καταδικάσαι ἀλλότριον ἡγούμενος τῆς σῆς δυνάμεως

text_en: For your power is the beginning of justice : and because you are Lord of all, you make yourself gracious to all.
text_la: Virtus enim tua justitiæ initium est, et ob hoc quod Dominus es, omnibus te parcere facis.
text_el: ἡ γὰρ ἰσχύς σου δικαιοσύνης ἀρχή καὶ τὸ πάντων σε δεσπόζειν πάντων φείδεσθαί σε ποιεῖ

text_en: For you show your power, when men will not believe you to be absolute in power, and you convince the boldness of them that know you not.
text_la: Virtutem enim ostendis tu, qui non crederis esse in virtute consummatus, et horum qui te nesciunt audaciam traducis.
text_el: ἰσχὺν γὰρ ἐνδείκνυσαι ἀπιστούμενος ἐπὶ δυνάμεως τελειότητι καὶ ἐν τοῖς εἰδόσι τὸ θράσος ἐξελέγχεις

text_en: But you being master of power, judge with tranquillity, and with great favour dispose of us: for your power is at hand when you will.
text_la: Tu autem dominator virtutis, cum tranquillitate judicas, et cum magna reverentia disponis nos : subest enim tibi, cum volueris posse.
text_el: σὺ δὲ δεσπόζων ἰσχύος ἐν ἐπιεικείᾳ κρίνεις καὶ μετὰ πολλῆς φειδοῦς διοικεῖς ἡμᾶς πάρεστιν γάρ σοι ὅταν θέλῃς τὸ δύνασθαι

text_en: But you have taught your people by such works, that they must be just and humane, and have made your children to be of a good hope : because in judging, you give place for repentance for sins .
text_la: Docuisti autem populum tuum per talia opera, quoniam oportet justum esse et humanum; et bonæ spei fecisti filios tuos, quoniam judicans das locum in peccatis pœnitentiæ.
text_el: ἐδίδαξας δέ σου τὸν λαὸν διὰ τῶν τοιούτων ἔργων ὅτι δεῖ τὸν δίκαιον εἶναι φιλάνθρωπον καὶ εὐέλπιδας ἐποίησας τοὺς υἱούς σου ὅτι διδοῖς ἐπὶ ἁμαρτήμασιν μετάνοιαν

text_en: For if you punished the enemies of your servants, and that deserved to die, with so great deliberation, giving them time and place whereby they might be changed from their wickedness :
text_la: Si enim inimicos servorum tuorum, et debitos morti, cum tanta cruciasti attentione, dans tempus et locum per quæ possent mutari a malitia :
text_el: εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὺς παίδων σου καὶ ὀφειλομένους θανάτῳ μετὰ τοσαύτης ἐτιμωρήσω προσοχῆς καὶ διέσεως δοὺς χρόνους καὶ τόπον δι' ὧν ἀπαλλαγῶσι τῆς κακίας

text_en: With what circumspection have you judged your own children, to whose parents you have sworn, and made covenants of good promises?
text_la: cum quanta diligentia judicasti filios tuos, quorum parentibus juramenta et conventiones dedisti bonarum promissionum!
text_el: μετὰ πόσης ἀκριβείας ἔκρινας τοὺς υἱούς σου ὧν τοῖς πατράσιν ὅρκους καὶ συνθήκας ἔδωκας ἀγαθῶν ὑποσχέσεων

text_en: Therefore whereas you chastise us, you scourge our enemies very many ways, to the end that when we judge we may think on your goodness : and when we are judged, we may hope for your mercy.
text_la: Cum ergo das nobis disciplinam, inimicos nostros multipliciter flagellas, ut bonitatem tuam cogitemus judicantes, et cum de nobis judicatur, speremus misericordiam tuam.
text_el: ἡμᾶς οὖν παιδεύων τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ἡμῶν ἐν μυριότητι μαστιγοῖς ἵνα σου τὴν ἀγαθότητα μεριμνῶμεν κρίνοντες κρινόμενοι δὲ προσδοκῶμεν ἔλεος

text_en: Wherefore you have also greatly tormented them, who, in their life, have lived foolishly and unjustly , by the same things which they worshipped.
text_la: Unde et illis qui in vita sua insensate et injuste vixerunt, per hæc quæ coluerunt dedisti summa tormenta.
text_el: ὅθεν καὶ τοὺς ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ ζωῆς βιώσαντας ἀδίκως διὰ τῶν ἰδίων ἐβασάνισας βδελυγμάτων

text_en: For they went astray for a long time in the ways of error , holding those things for gods which are the most worthless among beasts, living after the manner of children without understanding.
text_la: Etenim in erroris via diutius erraverunt, deos æstimantes hæc quæ in animalibus sunt supervacua, infantium insensatorum more viventes.
text_el: καὶ γὰρ τῶν πλάνης ὁδῶν μακρότερον ἐπλανήθησαν θεοὺς ὑπολαμβάνοντες τὰ καὶ ἐν ζῴοις τῶν αἰσχρῶν ἄτιμα νηπίων δίκην ἀφρόνων ψευσθέντες

text_en: Therefore you have sent a judgment upon them, as senseless children, to mock them.
text_la: Propter hoc tamquam pueris insensatis judicium in derisum dedisti.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο ὡς παισὶν ἀλογίστοις τὴν κρίσιν εἰς ἐμπαιγμὸν ἔπεμψας

text_en: But they that were not amended by mockeries and reprehensions, experienced the worthy judgment of God .
text_la: Qui autem ludibriis et increpationibus non sunt correcti, dignum Dei judicium experti sunt.
text_el: οἱ δὲ παιγνίοις ἐπιτιμήσεως μὴ νουθετηθέντες ἀξίαν θεοῦ κρίσιν πειράσουσιν

text_en: For seeing, with indignation, that they suffered by those very things which they took for gods, when they were destroyed by the same, they acknowledged him the true God , whom in time past they denied that they knew : for which cause the end also of their condemnation came upon them.
text_la: In quibus enim patientes indignabantur per hæc quos putabant deos, in ipsis cum exterminarentur videntes, illum quem olim negabant se nosse, verum Deum agnoverunt; propter quod et finis condemnationis eorum venit super illos.
text_el: ἐφ' οἷς γὰρ αὐτοὶ πάσχοντες ἠγανάκτουν ἐπὶ τούτοις οὓς ἐδόκουν θεούς ἐν αὐτοῖς κολαζόμενοι ἰδόντες ὃν πάλαι ἠρνοῦντο εἰδέναι θεὸν ἐπέγνωσαν ἀληθῆ διὸ καὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς καταδίκης ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἐπῆλθεν

text_en: But all men are vain, in whom there is not the knowledge of God : and who by these good things that are seen, could not understand him that is, neither by attending to the works have acknowledged who was the workman:
text_la: Vani autem sunt omnes homines in quibus non subest scientia Dei; et de his quæ videntur bona, non potuerunt intelligere eum qui est, neque operibus attendentes agnoverunt quis esset artifex :
text_el: μάταιοι μὲν γὰρ πάντες ἄνθρωποι φύσει οἷς παρῆν θεοῦ ἀγνωσία καὶ ἐκ τῶν ὁρωμένων ἀγαθῶν οὐκ ἴσχυσαν εἰδέναι τὸν ὄντα οὔτε τοῖς ἔργοις προσέχοντες ἐπέγνωσαν τὸν τεχνίτην

text_en: But have imagined either the fire, or the wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the great water, or the sun and moon, to be the gods that rule the world.
text_la: sed aut ignem, aut spiritum, aut citatum aërem, aut gyrum stellarum, aut nimiam aquam, aut solem et lunam, rectores orbis terrarum deos putaverunt.
text_el: ἀλλ' ἢ πῦρ ἢ πνεῦμα ἢ ταχινὸν ἀέρα ἢ κύκλον ἄστρων ἢ βίαιον ὕδωρ ἢ φωστῆρας οὐρανοῦ πρυτάνεις κόσμου θεοὺς ἐνόμισαν

text_en: With whose beauty, if they, being delighted, took them to be gods: let them know how much the Lord of them is more beautiful than they: for the first author of beauty made all those things.
text_la: Quorum si specie delectati, deos putaverunt, sciant quanto his dominator eorum speciosior est : speciei enim generator hæc omnia constituit.
text_el: ὧν εἰ μὲν τῇ καλλονῇ τερπόμενοι ταῦτα θεοὺς ὑπελάμβανον γνώτωσαν πόσῳ τούτων ὁ δεσπότης ἐστὶ βελτίων ὁ γὰρ τοῦ κάλλους γενεσιάρχης ἔκτισεν αὐτά

text_en: Or if they admired their power, and their effects, let them understand by them, that he that made them, is mightier than they:
text_la: Aut si virtutem et opera eorum mirati sunt, intelligant ab illis quoniam qui hæc fecit fortior est illis :
text_el: εἰ δὲ δύναμιν καὶ ἐνέργειαν ἐκπλαγέντες νοησάτωσαν ἀπ' αὐτῶν πόσῳ ὁ κατασκευάσας αὐτὰ δυνατώτερός ἐστιν

text_en: For by the greatness of the beauty, and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen, so as to be known thereby.
text_la: a magnitudine enim speciei et creaturæ cognoscibiliter poterit creator horum videri.
text_el: ἐκ γὰρ μεγέθους καὶ καλλονῆς κτισμάτων ἀναλόγως ὁ γενεσιουργὸς αὐτῶν θεωρεῖται

text_en: But yet as to these they are less to be blamed. For they perhaps err , seeking God , and desirous to find him.
text_la: Sed tamen adhuc in his minor est querela; et hi enim fortasse errant, Deum quærentes, et volentes invenire.
text_el: ἀλλ' ὅμως ἐπὶ τούτοις μέμψις ἐστὶν ὀλίγη καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ τάχα πλανῶνται θεὸν ζητοῦντες καὶ θέλοντες εὑρεῖν

text_en: For being conversant among his works, they search: and they are persuaded that the things are good which are seen.
text_la: Etenim cum in operibus illius conversentur inquirunt, et persuasum habent quoniam bona sunt quæ videntur.
text_el: ἐν γὰρ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ ἀναστρεφόμενοι διερευνῶσιν καὶ πείθονται τῇ ὄψει ὅτι καλὰ τὰ βλεπόμενα

text_en: But then again they are not to be pardoned.
text_la: Iterum autem nec his debet ignosci.
text_el: πάλιν δ' οὐδ' αὐτοὶ συγγνωστοί

text_en: For if they were able to know so much as to make a judgment of the world: how did they not more easily find out the Lord thereof?
text_la: Si enim tantum potuerunt scire ut possent æstimare sæculum, quomodo hujus Dominum non facilius invenerunt?
text_el: εἰ γὰρ τοσοῦτον ἴσχυσαν εἰδέναι ἵνα δύνωνται στοχάσασθαι τὸν αἰῶνα τὸν τούτων δεσπότην πῶς τάχιον οὐχ εὗρον

text_en: But unhappy are they, and their hope is among the dead, who have called gods the works of the hand of men , gold and silver, the inventions of art, and the resemblances of beasts, or an unprofitable stone the work of an ancient hand.
text_la: Infelices autem sunt, et inter mortuos spes illorum est, qui appellaverunt deos opera manuum hominum : aurum et argentum, artis inventionem, et similitudines animalium, aut lapidem inutilem, opus manus antiquæ.
text_el: ταλαίπωροι δὲ καὶ ἐν νεκροῖς αἱ ἐλπίδες αὐτῶν οἵτινες ἐκάλεσαν θεοὺς ἔργα χειρῶν ἀνθρώπων χρυσὸν καὶ ἄργυρον τέχνης ἐμμελέτημα καὶ ἀπεικάσματα ζῴων ἢ λίθον ἄχρηστον χειρὸς ἔργον ἀρχαίας

text_en: Or if an artist, a carpenter, has cut down a tree proper for his use in the wood, and skilfully taken off all the bark thereof, and with his art, diligently forms a vessel profitable for the common uses of life,
text_la: Aut si quis artifex faber de silva lignum rectum secuerit, et hujus docte eradat omnem corticem, et arte sua usus diligenter fabricet vas utile in conversationem vitæ;
text_el: εἰ δὲ καί τις ὑλοτόμος τέκτων εὐκίνητον φυτὸν ἐκπρίσας περιέξυσεν εὐμαθῶς πάντα τὸν φλοιὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ τεχνησάμενος εὐπρεπῶς κατεσκεύασεν χρήσιμον σκεῦος εἰς ὑπηρεσίαν ζωῆς

text_en: and uses the chips of his work to dress his meat:
text_la: reliquiis autem ejus operis ad præparationem escæ abutatur,
text_el: τὰ δὲ ἀποβλήματα τῆς ἐργασίας εἰς ἑτοιμασίαν τροφῆς ἀναλώσας ἐνεπλήσθη

text_en: And taking what was left thereof, which is good for nothing, being a crooked piece of wood, and full of knots, carves it diligently when he has nothing else to do, and by the skill of his art fashions it, and makes it like the image of a man :
text_la: et reliquum horum quod ad nullos usus facit, lignum curvum et vorticibus plenum sculpat diligenter per vacuitatem suam, et per scientiam suæ artis figuret illud, et assimilet illud imagini hominis,
text_el: τὸ δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπόβλημα εἰς οὐθὲν εὔχρηστον ξύλον σκολιὸν καὶ ὄζοις συμπεφυκός λαβὼν ἔγλυψεν ἐν ἐπιμελείᾳ ἀργίας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπειρίᾳ συνέσεως ἐτύπωσεν αὐτό ἀπείκασεν αὐτὸ εἰκόνι ἀνθρώπου

text_en: Or the resemblance of some beast, laying it over with vermilion, and painting it red, and covering every spot that is in it:
text_la: aut alicui ex animalibus illud comparet : perliniens rubrica, et rubicundum faciens fuco colorem illius, et omnem maculam quæ in illo est perliniens;
text_el: ἢ ζῴῳ τινὶ εὐτελεῖ ὡμοίωσεν αὐτὸ καταχρίσας μίλτῳ καὶ φύκει ἐρυθήνας χρόαν αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν κηλῖδα τὴν ἐν αὐτῷ καταχρίσας

text_en: And makes a convenient dwelling place for it, and setting it in a wall, and fastening it with iron,
text_la: et faciat ei dignam habitationem, et in pariete ponens illud, et confirmans ferro
text_el: καὶ ποιήσας αὐτῷ αὐτοῦ ἄξιον οἴκημα ἐν τοίχῳ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἀσφαλισάμενος σιδήρῳ

text_en: providing for it, lest it should fall, knowing that it is unable to help itself: for it is an image, and has need of help.
text_la: ne forte cadat, prospiciens illi : sciens quoniam non potest adjuvare se : imago enim est, et opus est illi adjutorium.
text_el: ἵνα μὲν οὖν μὴ καταπέσῃ προενόησεν αὐτοῦ εἰδὼς ὅτι ἀδυνατεῖ ἑαυτῷ βοηθῆσαι καὶ γάρ ἐστιν εἰκὼν καὶ χρείαν ἔχει βοηθείας

text_en: And then makes prayer to it, enquiring concerning his substance, and his children, or his marriage. And he is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life:
text_la: Et de substantia sua, et de filiis suis, et de nuptiis votum faciens inquirit : non erubescit loqui cum illo qui sine anima est.
text_el: περὶ δὲ κτημάτων καὶ γάμων αὐτοῦ καὶ τέκνων προσευχόμενος οὐκ αἰσχύνεται τῷ ἀψύχῳ προσλαλῶν καὶ περὶ μὲν ὑγιείας τὸ ἀσθενὲς ἐπικαλεῖται

text_en: And for health he makes supplication to the weak, and for life prays to that which is dead, and for help calls upon that which is unprofitable:
text_la: Et pro sanitate quidem infirmum deprecatur, et pro vita rogat mortuum, et in adjutorium inutilem invocat.
text_el: περὶ δὲ ζωῆς τὸ νεκρὸν ἀξιοῖ περὶ δὲ ἐπικουρίας τὸ ἀπειρότατον ἱκετεύει περὶ δὲ ὁδοιπορίας τὸ μηδὲ βάσει χρῆσθαι δυνάμενον

text_en: And for a good journey he petitions him that cannot walk: and for getting, and for working, and for the event of all things he asks him that is unable to do anything.
text_la: Et pro itinere petit ab eo qui ambulare non potest; et de acquirendo, et de operando, et de omnium rerum eventu, petit ab eo qui in omnibus est inutilis.
text_el: περὶ δὲ πορισμοῦ καὶ ἐργασίας καὶ χειρῶν ἐπιτυχίας τὸ ἀδρανέστατον ταῖς χερσὶν εὐδράνειαν αἰτεῖται

text_en: Again, another designing to sail, and beginning to make his voyage through the raging waves, calls upon a piece of wood more frail than the wood that carries him.
text_la: Iterum alius navigare cogitans, et per feros fluctus iter facere incipiens, ligno portante se, fragilius lignum invocat.
text_el: πλοῦν τις πάλιν στελλόμενος καὶ ἄγρια μέλλων διοδεύειν κύματα τοῦ φέροντος αὐτὸν πλοίου σαθρότερον ξύλον ἐπιβοᾶται

text_en: For this the desire of gain devised, and the workman built it by his skill.
text_la: Illud enim cupiditas acquirendi excogitavit, et artifex sapientia fabricavit sua.
text_el: ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ὄρεξις πορισμῶν ἐπενόησεν τεχνῖτις δὲ σοφία κατεσκεύασεν

text_en: But your providence , O Father , governs it: for you have made a way even in the sea, and a most sure path among the waves,
text_la: Tua autem, Pater, providentia gubernat : quoniam dedisti et in mari viam, et inter fluctus semitam firmissimam,
text_el: ἡ δὲ σή πάτερ διακυβερνᾷ πρόνοια ὅτι ἔδωκας καὶ ἐν θαλάσσῃ ὁδὸν καὶ ἐν κύμασι τρίβον ἀσφαλῆ

text_en: showing that you are able to save out of all things, yea, though a man went to sea without art.
text_la: ostendens quoniam potens es ex omnibus salvare, etiam si sine arte aliquis adeat mare.
text_el: δεικνὺς ὅτι δύνασαι ἐκ παντὸς σῴζειν ἵνα κἂν ἄνευ τέχνης τις ἐπιβῇ

text_en: But that the works of your wisdom might not be idle: therefore men also trust their lives even to a little wood, and passing over the sea by ship, are saved.
text_la: Sed ut non essent vacua sapientiæ tuæ opera, propter hoc etiam et exiguo ligno credunt homines animas suas, et transeuntes mare per ratem liberati sunt.
text_el: θέλεις δὲ μὴ ἀργὰ εἶναι τὰ τῆς σοφίας σου ἔργα διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐλαχίστῳ ξύλῳ πιστεύουσιν ἄνθρωποι ψυχὰς καὶ διελθόντες κλύδωνα σχεδίᾳ διεσώθησαν

text_en: And from the beginning also, when the proud giants perished, the hope of the world fleeing to a vessel, which was governed by your hand, left to the world seed of generation.
text_la: Sed et ab initio cum perirent superbi gigantes, spes orbis terrarum ad ratem confugiens, remisit sæculo semen nativitatis quæ manu tua erat gubernata.
text_el: καὶ ἀρχῆς γὰρ ἀπολλυμένων ὑπερηφάνων γιγάντων ἡ ἐλπὶς τοῦ κόσμου ἐπὶ σχεδίας καταφυγοῦσα ἀπέλιπεν αἰῶνι σπέρμα γενέσεως τῇ σῇ κυβερνηθεῖσα χειρί

text_en: For blessed is the wood, by which justice comes
text_la: Benedictum est enim lignum per quod fit justitia;
text_el: εὐλόγηται γὰρ ξύλον δι' οὗ γίνεται δικαιοσύνη

text_en: but the idol that is made by hands, is cursed , as well it, as he that made it: he because he made it; and it because being frail it is called a god.
text_la: per manus autem quod fit idolum, maledictum est et ipsum, et qui fecit illud : quia ille quidem operatus est, illud autem cum esset fragile, deus cognominatus est.
text_el: τὸ χειροποίητον δέ ἐπικατάρατον αὐτὸ καὶ ὁ ποιήσας αὐτό ὅτι ὁ μὲν ἠργάζετο τὸ δὲ φθαρτὸν θεὸς ὠνομάσθη

text_en: But to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike.
text_la: Similiter autem odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus;
text_el: ἐν ἴσῳ γὰρ μισητὰ θεῷ καὶ ὁ ἀσεβῶν καὶ ἡ ἀσέβεια αὐτοῦ

text_en: For that which is made, together with him that made it, shall suffer torments.
text_la: etenim quod factum est, cum illo qui fecit tormenta patietur.
text_el: καὶ γὰρ τὸ πραχθὲν σὺν τῷ δράσαντι κολασθήσεται

text_en: Therefore there shall be no respect had even to the idols of the Gentiles : because the creatures of God are turned to an abomination, and a temptation to the souls of men , and a snare to the feet of the unwise.
text_la: Propter hoc et in idolis nationum non erit respectus, quoniam creaturæ Dei in odium factæ sunt, et in tentationem animabus hominum, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium.
text_el: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐν εἰδώλοις ἐθνῶν ἐπισκοπὴ ἔσται ὅτι ἐν κτίσματι θεοῦ εἰς βδέλυγμα ἐγενήθησαν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλα ψυχαῖς ἀνθρώπων καὶ εἰς παγίδα ποσὶν ἀφρόνων

text_en: For the beginning of fornication is the devising of idols : and the invention of them is the corruption of life.
text_la: Initium enim fornicationis est exquisitio idolorum, et adinventio illorum corruptio vitæ est :
text_el: ἀρχὴ γὰρ πορνείας ἐπίνοια εἰδώλων εὕρεσις δὲ αὐτῶν φθορὰ ζωῆς

text_en: For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever.
text_la: neque enim erant ab initio, neque erunt in perpetuum.
text_el: οὔτε γὰρ ἦν ἀπ' ἀρχῆς οὔτε εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἔσται

text_en: For by the vanity of men they came into the world: and therefore they shall be found to come shortly to an end.
text_la: Supervacuitas enim hominum hæc advenit in orbem terrarum, et ideo brevis illorum finis est inventus.
text_el: κενοδοξίᾳ γὰρ ἀνθρώπων εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον καὶ διὰ τοῦτο σύντομον αὐτῶν τὸ τέλος ἐπενοήθη

text_en: For a father being afflicted with bitter grief, made to himself the image of his son, who was quickly taken away: and him who then had died as a man , he began now to worship as a god, and appointed him rites and sacrifices among his servants.
text_la: Acerbo enim luctu dolens pater, cito sibi rapti filii fecit imaginem; et illum qui tunc quasi homo mortuus fuerat, nunc tamquam deum colere cœpit, et constituit inter servos suos sacra et sacrificia.
text_el: ἀώρῳ γὰρ πένθει τρυχόμενος πατὴρ τοῦ ταχέως ἀφαιρεθέντος τέκνου εἰκόνα ποιήσας τόν ποτε νεκρὸν ἄνθρωπον νῦν ὡς θεὸν ἐτίμησεν καὶ παρέδωκεν τοῖς ὑποχειρίοις μυστήρια καὶ τελετάς

text_en: Then, in process of time, wicked custom prevailing, this error was kept as a law, and statues were worshipped by the commandment of tyrants.
text_la: Deinde interveniente tempore, convalescente iniqua consuetudine, hic error tamquam lex custoditus est, et tyrannorum imperio colebantur figmenta.
text_el: εἶτα ἐν χρόνῳ κρατυνθὲν τὸ ἀσεβὲς ἔθος ὡς νόμος ἐφυλάχθη

text_en: And those whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt far off, they brought their resemblance from afar, and made an express image of the king, whom they had a mind to honour : that by this their diligence, they might honour as present, him that was absent.
text_la: Et hos quos in palam homines honorare non poterant propter hoc quod longe essent, e longinquo figura eorum allata, evidentem imaginem regis quem honorare volebant fecerunt, ut illum qui aberat, tamquam præsentem colerent sua sollicitudine.
text_el: καὶ τυράννων ἐπιταγαῖς ἐθρησκεύετο τὰ γλυπτά οὓς ἐν ὄψει μὴ δυνάμενοι τιμᾶν ἄνθρωποι διὰ τὸ μακρὰν οἰκεῖν τὴν πόρρωθεν ὄψιν ἀνατυπωσάμενοι ἐμφανῆ εἰκόνα τοῦ τιμωμένου βασιλέως ἐποίησαν ἵνα ὡς παρόντα τὸν ἀπόντα κολακεύωσιν διὰ τῆς σπουδῆς

text_en: And to the worshipping of these, the singular diligence also of the artificer helped to set forward the ignorant .
text_la: Provexit autem ad horum culturam et hos qui ignorabant artificis eximia diligentia.
text_el: εἰς ἐπίτασιν δὲ θρησκείας καὶ τοὺς ἀγνοοῦντας ἡ τοῦ τεχνίτου προετρέψατο φιλοτιμία

text_en: For he being willing to please him that employed him, laboured with all his art to make the resemblance in the best manner.
text_la: Ille enim, volens placere illi qui se assumpsit, elaboravit arte sua ut similitudinem in melius figuraret.
text_el: ὁ μὲν γὰρ τάχα κρατοῦντι βουλόμενος ἀρέσαι ἐξεβιάσατο τῇ τέχνῃ τὴν ὁμοιότητα ἐπὶ τὸ κάλλιον

text_en: And the multitude of men , carried away by the beauty of the work, took him now for a god, that little before was but honoured as a man .
text_la: Multitudo autem hominum, abducta per speciem operis, eum qui ante tempus tamquam homo honoratus fuerat, nunc deum æstimaverunt.
text_el: τὸ δὲ πλῆθος ἐφελκόμενον διὰ τὸ εὔχαρι τῆς ἐργασίας τὸν πρὸ ὀλίγου τιμηθέντα ἄνθρωπον νῦν σέβασμα ἐλογίσαντο

text_en: And this was the occasion of deceiving human life: for men serving either their affection, or their kings, gave the incommunicable name to stones and wood.
text_la: Et hæc fuit vitæ humanæ deceptio, quoniam aut affectui aut regibus deservientes homines, incommunicabile nomen lapidibus et lignis imposuerunt.
text_el: καὶ τοῦτο ἐγένετο τῷ βίῳ εἰς ἔνεδρον ὅτι ἢ συμφορᾷ ἢ τυραννίδι δουλεύσαντες ἄνθρωποι τὸ ἀκοινώνητον ὄνομα λίθοις καὶ ξύλοις περιέθεσαν

text_en: And it was not enough for them to err about the knowledge of God , but whereas they lived in a great war of ignorance , they call so many and so great evils peace.
text_la: Et non suffecerat errasse eos circa Dei scientiam, sed et in magno viventes inscientiæ bello, tot et tam magna mala pacem appellant.
text_el: εἶτ' οὐκ ἤρκεσεν τὸ πλανᾶσθαι περὶ τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ γνῶσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν μεγάλῳ ζῶντες ἀγνοίας πολέμῳ τὰ τοσαῦτα κακὰ εἰρήνην προσαγορεύουσιν

text_en: For either they sacrifice their own children, or use hidden sacrifices , or keep watches full of madness ,
text_la: Aut enim filios suos sacrificantes, aut obscura sacrificia facientes, aut insaniæ plenas vigilias habentes,
text_el: ἢ γὰρ τεκνοφόνους τελετὰς ἢ κρύφια μυστήρια ἢ ἐμμανεῖς ἐξάλλων θεσμῶν κώμους ἄγοντες

text_en: so that now they neither keep life, nor marriage undefiled, but one kills another through envy , or grieves him by adultery :
text_la: neque vitam, neque nuptias mundas jam custodiunt : sed alius alium per invidiam occidit, aut adulterans contristat,
text_el: οὔτε βίους οὔτε γάμους καθαροὺς ἔτι φυλάσσουσιν ἕτερος δ' ἕτερον ἢ λοχῶν ἀναιρεῖ ἢ νοθεύων ὀδυνᾷ

text_en: And all things are mingled together, blood, murder , theft , and dissimulation, corruption and unfaithfulness, tumults and perjury , disquieting of the good ,
text_la: et omnia commista sunt : sanguis, homicidium, furtum et fictio, corruptio et infidelitas, turbatio et perjurium, tumultus bonorum,
text_el: πάντα δ' ἐπιμὶξ ἔχει αἷμα καὶ φόνος κλοπὴ καὶ δόλος φθορά ἀπιστία τάραχος ἐπιορκία

text_en: forgetfulness of God , defiling of souls , changing of nature, disorder in marriage, and the irregularity of adultery and uncleanness .
text_la: Dei immemoratio, animarum inquinatio, nativitatis immutatio, nuptiarum inconstantia, inordinatio mœchiæ et impudicitiæ.
text_el: θόρυβος ἀγαθῶν χάριτος ἀμνηστία ψυχῶν μιασμός γενέσεως ἐναλλαγή γάμων ἀταξία μοιχεία καὶ ἀσέλγεια

text_en: For the worship of abominable idols is the cause, and the beginning and end of all evil .
text_la: Infandorum enim idolorum cultura omnis mali causa est, et initium et finis.
text_el: ἡ γὰρ τῶν ἀνωνύμων εἰδώλων θρησκεία παντὸς ἀρχὴ κακοῦ καὶ αἰτία καὶ πέρας ἐστίν

text_en: For either they are mad when they are merry: or they prophesy lies, or they live unjustly , or easily forswear themselves.
text_la: Aut enim dum lætantur insaniunt, aut certe vaticinantur falsa, aut vivunt injuste, aut pejerant cito.
text_el: ἢ γὰρ εὐφραινόμενοι μεμήνασιν ἢ προφητεύουσιν ψευδῆ ἢ ζῶσιν ἀδίκως ἢ ἐπιορκοῦσιν ταχέως

text_en: For whilst they trust in idols , which are without life, though they swear amiss, they look not to be hurt.
text_la: Dum enim confidunt in idolis quæ sine anima sunt, male jurantes noceri se non sperant.
text_el: ἀψύχοις γὰρ πεποιθότες εἰδώλοις κακῶς ὀμόσαντες ἀδικηθῆναι οὐ προσδέχονται

text_en: But for both these things they shall be justly punished, because they have thought not well of God , giving heed to idols , and have sworn unjustly , in guile despising justice .
text_la: Utraque ergo illis evenient digne, quoniam male senserunt de Deo, attendentes idolis, et juraverunt injuste, in dolo contemnentes justitiam.
text_el: ἀμφότερα δὲ αὐτοὺς μετελεύσεται τὰ δίκαια ὅτι κακῶς ἐφρόνησαν περὶ θεοῦ προσέχοντες εἰδώλοις καὶ ἀδίκως ὤμοσαν ἐν δόλῳ καταφρονήσαντες ὁσιότητος

text_en: For it is not the power of them, by whom they swear , but the just vengeance of sinners always punishes the transgression of the unjust .
text_la: Non enim juratorum virtus, sed peccantium pœna, perambulat semper injustorum prævaricationem.
text_el: οὐ γὰρ ἡ τῶν ὀμνυμένων δύναμις ἀλλ' ἡ τῶν ἁμαρτανόντων δίκη ἐπεξέρχεται ἀεὶ τὴν τῶν ἀδίκων παράβασιν

text_en: But you, our God , are gracious and true , patient, and ordering all things in mercy.
text_la: Tu autem, Deus noster, suavis et verus es, patiens, et in misericordia disponens omnia.
text_el: σὺ δέ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν χρηστὸς καὶ ἀληθής μακρόθυμος καὶ ἐλέει διοικῶν τὰ πάντα

text_en: For if we sin , we are yours, knowing your greatness: and if we sin not, we know that we are counted with you.
